DEPTH-FIRST SEARCH (DFS) AND BREADTH-FIRST SEARCH (BFS) ARE BOTH GRAPH TRAVERSAL ALGORITHMS BUT DIFFER IN THEIR APPROACH. DFS EXPLORES AS FAR AS POSSIBLE ALONG EACH BRANCH BEFORE BACKTRACKING, WHILE BFS EXPLORES ALL NEIGHBORS AT THE CURRENT DEPTH LEVEL BEFORE MOVING TO THE NEXT LEVEL. DFS USES A STACK (LIFO) STRUCTURE, AND BFS USES A QUEUE (FIFO) STRUCTURE. 

YOU WOULD CHOOSE DFS WHEN THE SOLUTION IS LIKELY TO BE DEEP IN THE GRAPH OR WHEN MEMORY USAGE IS A CONCERN (SINCE DFS ONLY STORES THE CURRENT PATH). BFS IS PREFERRED WHEN THE SOLUTION IS NEAR THE START NODE OR WHEN YOU NEED TO FIND THE SHORTEST PATH IN AN UNWEIGHTED GRAPH. ADDITIONALLY, BFS AVOIDS INFINITE LOOPS MORE RELIABLY WITH A VISITED SET, WHILE DFS CAN GET STUCK IN CYCLES IF NOT PROPERLY IMPLEMENTED.
